newsitem.title: USA: ARCO to buy Elf Aquitaine's Tunisia assets.
newsitem.headline: ARCO to buy Elf Aquitaine's Tunisia assets.

text.p: Atlantic Richfield Co (ARCO) agreed on Monday to buy French oil giant Elf Aquitaine's oil fields in Tunisia.
Terms of the deal were not disclosed, an ARCO spokesman told Reuters.
The acquisitions, including a 50 percent interest in the offshore Ashtart oilfield, will add 25 million barrels of oil to ARCO's proved reserves this year, the company said in a statement.
Ashtart contains 800 million barrels of oil in place and has producted 240 million barrels since its discovery in 1971.
Ashtart is jointly owned by Elf Hydrocarbures Tunisie, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Elf Aquitaine, and ETAP, the Tunisian national oil company, each with a 50 percent interest.
The field is operated by SEREPT, a joint operating company of Elf Aquitaine and ETAP.
As part of the transaction, which is expected to close in August subject to government approvals, ARCO will acquire EHT's interest share of SEREPT.

"We are excited by Ashtart because of its enhanced oil recovery potential and the exploration upside that could increase reserves significantly," said Jay Cheatham, president of ARCO International Oil and GAs Company.
